Summary adjusted with SLOOS insights:
- The FOMC’s June 14, 2017 statement is cautiously optimistic: continued labor-market strength, moderate growth, below-target inflation, a 25 bp rate hike to 1–1.25%, and plans to begin gradual balance-sheet normalization while keeping policy accommodative.
- April 2017 SLOOS points to mixed credit supply: banks reported tighter standards in auto lending and continued caution in CRE, while easing in credit card standards and increased willingness to make consumer installment loans provided some offset. Foreign banks reportedly increased loan-rate spreads and used interest-rate floors, implying somewhat firmer pricing. These elements suggest marginal headwinds from bank credit, even as household credit availability remains supportive in some segments.
- Incorporating SLOOS, financial conditions look a touch less accommodative than the FOMC statement alone implies. Net tone remains mildly positive, but tempered by pockets of tightening and below-target inflation.
